events.summary:
H1 is the best-supported hypothesis: the temporal ordering is clean and verified (exchange-gateway's first error 11:01:25Z precedes order-service's first error 11:02:45Z), the error signature is homogeneous and dependency-shaped (349/349 order-service errors are 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout'), the ~5.2s p99 plateau matches exchange-gateway's 5000ms connect timeout, exchange-gateway's upstream latency to api.exchange-partner.example rose ~119ms -> ~9.2s, and order-service's own resources are flat with 0 restarts. The rollback at 11:16Z changes nothing (flat ~30-31% step from 11:02Z through 12:55Z), which independently kills H2/H5 as the sustaining cause and is consistent with H1. H3 and H4 are contradicted by the homogeneous, partner-named error signature and the absence of any db/cache/kafka signature.

However, the load-bearing hop of H1 — that the 11:01:25Z partner timeouts are genuine *external provider* degradation rather than a fault inside exchange-gateway (client-side saturation, connection pool/deploy, or network path) — rests on an explicit assumption with no corroborating evidence: no partner-side telemetry exists (unavailable, do not re-request), exchange-gateway's own resource/connection metrics were never queried, and only exchange-gateway's client-observed symptoms were sampled (truncated). H1 also cannot explain scope beyond order-service + exchange-gateway, because no other service was checked. Separately, a genuine amplifier variant of H2 remains untested: whether exchange-gateway's request volume/mix to the partner changed at 10:48-11:02Z (retry amplification from the new submit handler). That is obtainable and could add order-service as a contributing cause even if the partner is the origin.

These are obtainable and would change trust in (or the ranking of) H1, so I am sending two focused requests rather than accepting. If exchange-gateway is healthy on its own resource/connection metrics and shows no traffic-shape change, and at least one other exchange-partner caller is failing at the same time, H1 can be accepted at higher confidence.

H2's amplifier form is directly refuted by the flat request_rate [F22,F23]; H3 is refuted because pricing-engine — the config-changed component and order-service's direct callee — is flat (0.15-0.26%, zero ERROR logs) while its own downstream market-data-service degrades, inverting propagation [F30]; H4/H5 have no supporting signature (no db/cache/kafka error text, order-service resources flat, plateau invariant across the rollback) [F9,F12,F15].

Residual gaps are non-blocking: partner-side telemetry does not exist and cannot be requested; exchange-gateway exposes no pool/executor metric (only qualitative healthy logs); market-data-service and api-gateway ERROR logs were not retrieved, so the shared-partner mechanism for those two is inference from same-timed steps rather than confirmed error text. Also, the 'genuine external provider' vs 'network path between gateway and partner' distinction is unresolvable and immaterial — both are external to the stack and neither implicates any changeable component. critiques.summary:
H1 is the best-supported hypothesis: the temporal ordering is clean and verified (exchange-gateway's first error 11:01:25Z precedes order-service's first error 11:02:45Z), the error signature is homogeneous and dependency-shaped (349/349 order-service errors are 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout'), the ~5.2s p99 plateau matches exchange-gateway's 5000ms connect timeout, exchange-gateway's upstream latency to api.exchange-partner.example rose ~119ms -> ~9.2s, and order-service's own resources are flat with 0 restarts. The rollback at 11:16Z changes nothing (flat ~30-31% step from 11:02Z through 12:55Z), which independently kills H2/H5 as the sustaining cause and is consistent with H1. H3 and H4 are contradicted by the homogeneous, partner-named error signature and the absence of any db/cache/kafka signature.

However, the load-bearing hop of H1 — that the 11:01:25Z partner timeouts are genuine *external provider* degradation rather than a fault inside exchange-gateway (client-side saturation, connection pool/deploy, or network path) — rests on an explicit assumption with no corroborating evidence: no partner-side telemetry exists (unavailable, do not re-request), exchange-gateway's own resource/connection metrics were never queried, and only exchange-gateway's client-observed symptoms were sampled (truncated). H1 also cannot explain scope beyond order-service + exchange-gateway, because no other service was checked. Separately, a genuine amplifier variant of H2 remains untested: whether exchange-gateway's request volume/mix to the partner changed at 10:48-11:02Z (retry amplification from the new submit handler). That is obtainable and could add order-service as a contributing cause even if the partner is the origin.

These are obtainable and would change trust in (or the ranking of) H1, so I am sending two focused requests rather than accepting. If exchange-gateway is healthy on its own resource/connection metrics and shows no traffic-shape change, and at least one other exchange-partner caller is failing at the same time, H1 can be accepted at higher confidence.

challenges.issue: The pivotal hop — 'the 11:01:25Z connect timeouts/503s reflect genuine external provider degradation rather than a client-side/network fault inside exchange-gateway' — is an explicit ASSUMPTION, not a verified finding. All partner-side evidence is exchange-gateway's own client-side view (its logs, its upstream_latency_ms); no exchange-gateway resource metrics (cpu, memory, connection/thread pool, restarts) or network/error-rate metrics were queried. exchange-gateway p99 rose to ~5.2s and its latency to the partner to ~9.2s, but a saturated/blocked exchange-gateway would produce the same client-side picture. F10/F16/F17/F18 support 'the fault is at or beyond exchange-gateway', not specifically 'the partner is at fault'.

Scope is unverified: the hypothesis claims order-service is a victim of a partner-wide problem, but no other caller of api.exchange-partner.example (or of exchange-gateway) was checked. If only order-service/exchange-gateway are affected, a call-pattern or client-side explanation regains weight; a partner-wide failure would confirm H1 and kill H2/H3. The blast-radius claim is currently inferred from two services only.

Supporting evidence relies on truncated log pulls (exchange-gateway 30/34 returned; order-service 40/349 returned). The 'all errors are the same signature' claim is strong but partially censored; the absence of any other signature after the 11:16Z rollback is not proven.

The rejected/ranked hypothesis was not fully tested in its survivable form: the claim that the new order-service retry-safe submit handler caused retry amplification or an altered call pattern toward exchange-gateway was never tested. Exchange-gateway's request volume/mix to the partner at 10:48-11:02Z is obtainable and would either revive H2 as a contributing amplifier or firmly reject it. Note this does not threaten H1's verdict that the *origin* is the partner, but it threatens the 'order-service is purely a victim' framing and the confidence in dismissing the deploy entirely.

Rejected largely by the homogeneity of the order-service error signature, which is sound. But the 'redis-cache never degraded' claim rests on a telemetry gap (never queried) rather than a negative finding; HIST-107 leaves residual doubt. Low priority given F9/F15/F16/F18, so not blocking.

Dismissal is well-reasoned on the error-signature argument, but the 'no infra event' conclusion partly rests on absence of evidence from change APIs that explicitly cannot surface infra events (F7 caveat). Acceptable as-is because the positive error-signature evidence carries the rejection.

critiques.summary:
H1 is now adequately supported and all competing hypotheses are contradicted by verified evidence. The causal chain is grounded end-to-end: (1) onset is a clean step, not a ramp — order-service error rate 0.11-0.32% through 11:01Z then 30.97% at 11:02Z and steady ~30-31% through 12:55Z [F8]; (2) the failure is entirely dependency-shaped — 349/349 order-service ERROR lines are 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' [F9,F15]; (3) the ordering is tight and correct — exchange-gateway's first error is 11:01:25Z, ~80s BEFORE order-service's 11:02:45Z [F10,F16,F24,F13]; (4) the failing hop is isolated to the partner — exchange-gateway is NOT saturated (cpu 27.7-31.1% flat, memory 42-48%, 0 restarts, 'connection pool stats: healthy' 10:48/10:58Z, 'health check ok' 11:02Z) and 100% of its ERROR lines are partner-facing timeouts/503s against host=api.exchange-partner.example with upstream_latency stepping 119ms -> ~9.2s [F18,F20,F21,F25,F27]; (5) volume is flat, killing the retry-amplification hop — exchange-gateway inbound request_rate is 250-292 req/s (mean 272) with no surge at the 10:48Z deploy or onset; only call QUALITY changed, upstream_error_rate 0.3% -> 45% [F22,F23]; (6) scope now extends beyond the reported path — market-data-service (0.25% -> 3.4%) and api-gateway (0.26% -> 3.2%) step at the same 11:00Z bucket with no local fault signature [F28,F29,F31]; (7) the intervention test is decisive — the 11:16Z rollback changes nothing (flat ~30-31% across the boundary, unchanged partner-named signature, upstream latency predating and outlasting it) [F8,F9,F18]. H2's amplifier form is directly refuted by the flat request_rate [F22,F23]; H3 is refuted because pricing-engine — the config-changed component and order-service's direct callee — is flat (0.15-0.26%, zero ERROR logs) while its own downstream market-data-service degrades, inverting propagation [F30]; H4/H5 have no supporting signature (no db/cache/kafka error text, order-service resources flat, plateau invariant across the rollback) [F9,F12,F15].

Residual gaps are non-blocking: partner-side telemetry does not exist and cannot be requested; exchange-gateway exposes no pool/executor metric (only qualitative healthy logs); market-data-service and api-gateway ERROR logs were not retrieved, so the shared-partner mechanism for those two is inference from same-timed steps rather than confirmed error text. Also, the 'genuine external provider' vs 'network path between gateway and partner' distinction is unresolvable and immaterial — both are external to the stack and neither implicates any changeable component. No further query would flip which hypothesis ranks first, and further rounds cost minutes during a SEV-1.

challenges.issue: The load-bearing hop — that the 11:01:25Z partner timeouts are genuine external provider degradation — still rests on client-side observation only, since no partner-side telemetry exists. However this no longer bears weight: exchange-gateway's own health is verified (flat cpu/memory, 0 restarts, healthy pool logs, 100% partner-facing ERROR lines) and the competing in-stack alternatives are each contradicted, so the remaining ambiguity is external-provider vs external-network-path, both non-actionable, non-internal, and outside any controllable component. Downgraded from blocking to minor.

Scope rest is partly inferential: market-data-service and api-gateway show same-timed error steps [F28,F29] but their ERROR logs were never retrieved, so it is not verified that their errors are partner-facing timeouts rather than a coincident unrelated cause. Additionally market-data-service is not on the order-service call path per the dependency map, so the 'partner-wide' generalization for that service is inference, not proof. This affects breadth of the blast-radius claim, not the identity of the origin for order-service/exchange-gateway.

No deploy/version marker was found in any telemetry, so H1's chain cannot positively exclude v2.15.2 as a coincidentally simultaneous change. But this does not weaken H1: the failure onset is 80s earlier at exchange-gateway, the rollback at 11:16Z produces zero change in the error plateau, and the fault text is partner-named throughout — so a release-driven cause would have to explain all three, which no evidence supports.

The first causal hop ('the rollout alters how submit calls exchange-gateway') remains evidence-free as flagged by the automated check. Not blocking: both the origin form (partner timeouts precede any order-service error, failures appear in services order-service does not call) and the amplifier form (flat 250-292 req/s inbound at exchange-gateway across 10:48Z and onset) are refuted. Note the residual limitation that exchange-gateway exposes no per-caller request split, so order-service's individual outbound rate is inferred from the flat aggregate rather than measured.

Infrastructure events (failovers, IOPS throttling, capacity) are structurally invisible to the deploy/config APIs, so H4 cannot be positively excluded by absence of a recorded change [F7]. It is nevertheless contradicted positively: no db/cache/kafka error signature appears, order-service resources are flat with 0 restarts, and all failures are partner-named — so it survives only as an unfalsifiable residual, not a competing explanation.

redis-cache degradation was never directly queried (the HIST-107 precedent path), so H3's mechanism is rejected on propagation-direction grounds and error-signature grounds rather than by direct redis telemetry. Non-blocking because the config-changed component's own direct callee path shows zero degradation.
